question: A ward has a record 12 resistant-bacteria infections one year, launches a hand-gel campaign, then has 6 the next. What does that show?
options: Little, since record years tend to fall back
The campaign failed, as 6 is still many
answer: Little, on its own. A campaign launched after a record year starts at a peak, and peaks are partly bad luck, so the next year tends to be lower anyway. With counts this small, 12 to 6 is within chance. The test is a similar ward without the campaign, over several years.
move: Measure a fix started at a peak against places that did nothing.
trap: Crediting the campaign because it followed the worst year on record.
source: Barnett et al., Int J Epidemiology, 2005
reference: Barnett, van der Pols & Dobson, Regression to the mean: what it is and how to deal with it, International Journal of Epidemiology, 2005
